# Koreada Ta'lim (koreadatalim.com)

> Koreada Ta'lim ("Education in Korea" in Uzbek) is a study-in-Korea admission and student visa consultancy for students from Uzbekistan and the Uzbek diaspora worldwide. It is run by Ikhlos Khamidov, an Uzbek international student in South Korea who worked for 2+ years in a Korean university's international office. Since 2023 he has helped 70+ students get admitted to Korean universities and receive D-4 and D-2 student visas. The first consultation is free. Consultations in Uzbek, English and Korean; the website is available in Uzbek (Latin and Cyrillic), Russian and English.

## Key facts

- Name: Koreada Ta'lim (also written "Koreada Talim", "KoreadaTalim")
- Founder: Ikhlos Khamidov — studies Global Communication and Business Administration at Seowon University (Cheongju, South Korea); graduated from the lyceum of the University of World Economy and Diplomacy (Tashkent); 2+ years handling visas and documents for international students in a university international office
- Active since: 2023
- Students helped: 70+
- Based in: South Korea; serves Uzbekistan and Uzbeks living abroad (Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkey and elsewhere); consultations and applications are done online
- Policy: does not promise a "visa guarantee" — the final decision is made by immigration; the service focuses on correct, complete documents to reduce refusal risk

## Services

- Korean language courses at universities (D-4 visa), including telex visa route
- Bachelor's degree applications (D-2 visa): choosing university and major, application, personal statement
- Master's degree applications (D-2 / e-visa): program choice, document package, e-visa
- Vocational education programs
- Student visa document preparation and checking
- D-4 to D-2 visa change for language students already in Korea
- Airport pickup (Incheon) and housing help for students with approved visas
- Free first consultation

## Universities applied to

Chungbuk National University (충북대학교), Seowon University (서원대학교), Korea Aerospace University (한국항공대학교), Chungbuk Provincial University (충북도립대학교), Kyonggi University (경기대학교), Hanbat National University (국립한밭대학교), Kongju National University (국립공주대학교), Hoseo University (호서대학교), Chungcheong University (충청대학교), Gwangju Women's University (광주여자대학교), Yewon Arts University (예원예술대학교), Woongji Accounting & Tax College (웅지세무대학교), DK University, Daejeon Institute of Science and Technology, Sudo International University, Korea Bible University.

## Student results (examples)

- IELTS 7 → Chungbuk National University with a 70% scholarship, e-visa approved without bank statement / annual income documents
- TOPIK 2 → K-Beauty master's at Gwangju Women's University with an 80% scholarship; e-visa approved in 7 days
- IELTS → Engineering at Korea Aerospace University (the only one selected out of 60 Uzbek applicants)
- TOPIK 3 → Business at Seowon University, D-2 visa
- No language certificate, older applicant → Kyonggi University (Seoul), e-visa approved

## Quick answers

- D-4 vs D-2: D-4 is the visa for Korean language programs at universities; D-2 is for bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees. Many students start on D-4 and switch to D-2 inside Korea.
- Intakes: university language programs usually start in March, June, September and December; degree programs start in March (spring) and September (fall). Start preparing 4–6 months ahead.
- Korean language not required to start: most students begin with a language course.
- Scholarships: many universities give tuition discounts based on TOPIK or IELTS level.
